Class FakeRandom

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.testing.FakeRandom
All Implemented Interfaces:
RandomGenerator
public final class FakeRandom extends Object implements RandomGenerator
A RandomGenerator that gives the numbers a test scripted, in order, so that tests of code that uses randomness are exact. 
var random = new FakeRandom().addFaces(6, 1, 4, 4);
var rolled = DiceExpression.parse("4d6dl1").roll(random);
assertThat(rolled.value()).isEqualTo(14);
assertThat(random.isExhausted()).isTrue();

A scripted number is of one of two kinds:

  • An exact value, added with one of the add methods, is given as it is to a call that returns its type: an int to nextInt, with or without bounds, a long to nextLong, a double to nextDouble(), and a boolean to nextBoolean().
  • A fraction, added with addFractions(double...), is given to any call, as the value at that fraction of what the call may return: 0.5 is 3 to nextInt(6) and 0.5 to nextDouble(). To nextLong(), it's the 64 bits that are at that fraction of 2^64 when read as an unsigned number, which is how a weighted RandomSelector reads them.

A call fails with IllegalStateException when no number is left, when the next one is an exact value of another type, or when it's out of the bounds of the call: the code under test doesn't use randomness as the test expects. The other methods of RandomGenerator are built on these ones.

It isn't thread-safe.
